# MODULE 23: Generative Models — Autoencoders, VAEs, GANs & Diffusion Models

### _ELBO Derivation, GAN Minimax Theorem, Score Matching & DDPM_

---

## 23.1 Conceptual Overview

### The Generative Modeling Problem

All models in Modules 15–22 solve **discriminative** problems: given input $\mathbf{x}$, predict output $y$. Generative models solve the deeper problem: learn the distribution $p(\mathbf{x})$ itself. From this distribution we can:

- **Sample** new data points ($\mathbf{x} \sim p(\mathbf{x})$) — generate images, text, audio
- **Evaluate likelihoods** ($p(\mathbf{x})$) — detect anomalies, compress data
- **Perform conditional generation** ($p(\mathbf{x}\mid y)$) — text-to-image, image-to-image

The challenge is that natural data distributions are complex, high-dimensional, and multimodal — a distribution over natural images has modes at cats, dogs, landscapes, faces, and infinitely many other concepts, each a manifold in $\mathbb{R}^{3HW}$ pixel space.

### The Four Paradigms

Four families of generative models have emerged, each with a different approach to the fundamental tradeoff between **tractability** (can we evaluate $p(\mathbf{x})$ exactly?) and **flexibility** (can the model represent complex distributions?):

**Autoencoders:** Learn a compressed latent representation. Deterministic — not generative in the strict sense, but foundational.

**Variational Autoencoders (VAEs):** Replace the deterministic bottleneck with a probabilistic one. Maximize a lower bound on the log-likelihood. Tractable, flexible, but samples can be blurry.

**Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs):** Train a generator and discriminator in a minimax game. Implicit likelihood — we cannot evaluate $p(\mathbf{x})$ but can sample sharply. High quality but training instability.

**Diffusion Models:** Define a forward noising process and learn to reverse it. State-of-the-art image quality. Slower sampling but stable training and likelihood evaluation.

---

## 23.2 Mathematical Formalization

### 23.2.1 Autoencoders — The Representation Learning Foundation

An autoencoder trains an **encoder** $f_\phi: \mathcal{X} \to \mathcal{Z}$ and **decoder** $g_\theta: \mathcal{Z} \to \mathcal{X}$ to minimize reconstruction error:

$$\mathcal{L}_{\text{AE}}(\phi, \theta) = \mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{x}\sim p_{\text{data}}}[|\mathbf{x} - g_\theta(f_\phi(\mathbf{x}))|^2] \tag{23.1}$$

The bottleneck dimension $d_z \ll d_x$ forces the encoder to learn a compact, meaningful representation. The latent code $\mathbf{z} = f_\phi(\mathbf{x})$ captures the most information-theoretically relevant structure of $\mathbf{x}$.

**Why autoencoders are not generative:** There is no probabilistic model on $\mathcal{Z}$. Sampling $\mathbf{z} \sim \mathcal{N}(\mathbf{0},\mathbf{I})$ and decoding gives poor quality outputs because the latent space has no structure — regions between data embeddings are unmapped.

**Denoising Autoencoders:** Train to reconstruct $\mathbf{x}$ from corrupted input $\tilde{\mathbf{x}} = \mathbf{x} + \boldsymbol\varepsilon$: $$\mathcal{L}_{\text{DAE}} = \mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{x}, \boldsymbol\varepsilon}[|\mathbf{x} - g_\theta(f_\phi(\mathbf{x}+\boldsymbol\varepsilon))|^2] \tag{23.2}$$

Denoising autoencoders implicitly learn the **score function** $\nabla_\mathbf{x}\log p(\mathbf{x})$ — the key insight that later inspired diffusion models.

---

### 23.2.2 Variational Autoencoders — The ELBO Derivation

The VAE (Kingma & Welling, 2013) is a **latent variable model**. The generative model defines:

$$p_\theta(\mathbf{x}) = \int p_\theta(\mathbf{x}\mid\mathbf{z}),p(\mathbf{z}),d\mathbf{z} \tag{23.3}$$

where $p(\mathbf{z}) = \mathcal{N}(\mathbf{0},\mathbf{I})$ is a standard Gaussian prior and $p_\theta(\mathbf{x}\mid\mathbf{z})$ is the **decoder** (a neural network).

**The intractability problem:** Computing the marginal $p_\theta(\mathbf{x}) = \int p_\theta(\mathbf{x}\mid\mathbf{z})p(\mathbf{z})d\mathbf{z}$ requires integrating over all $\mathbf{z}$ — intractable for continuous high-dimensional $\mathbf{z}$.

**The posterior is also intractable:** $$p_\theta(\mathbf{z}\mid\mathbf{x}) = \frac{p_\theta(\mathbf{x}\mid\mathbf{z})p(\mathbf{z})}{p_\theta(\mathbf{x})}$$

Since $p_\theta(\mathbf{x})$ is intractable, so is the posterior.

**Solution: Variational Inference.** Introduce an **encoder** (recognition network) $q_\phi(\mathbf{z}\mid\mathbf{x})$ that approximates the true posterior $p_\theta(\mathbf{z}\mid\mathbf{x})$.

**Derivation of the ELBO:**

Starting from the log-likelihood: $$\log p_\theta(\mathbf{x}) = \log\int p_\theta(\mathbf{x}\mid\mathbf{z})p(\mathbf{z}),d\mathbf{z}$$

Multiply and divide by $q_\phi(\mathbf{z}\mid\mathbf{x})$: $$= \log\mathbb{E}_{q_\phi(\mathbf{z}\mid\mathbf{x})}!\left[\frac{p_\theta(\mathbf{x}\mid\mathbf{z})p(\mathbf{z})}{q_\phi(\mathbf{z}\mid\mathbf{x})}\right]$$

Apply Jensen's inequality (Module 3, Eq. 3.20) with the concave $\log$: $$\geq \mathbb{E}_{q_\phi(\mathbf{z}\mid\mathbf{x})}!\left[\log\frac{p_\theta(\mathbf{x}\mid\mathbf{z})p(\mathbf{z})}{q_\phi(\mathbf{z}\mid\mathbf{x})}\right] \tag{23.4}$$

This is the **Evidence Lower BOund (ELBO)**:

$$\log p_\theta(\mathbf{x}) \geq \mathcal{L}_{\text{ELBO}}(\phi, \theta; \mathbf{x}) = \underbrace{\mathbb{E}_{q_\phi}!\left[\log p_\theta(\mathbf{x}\mid\mathbf{z})\right]}_{\text{reconstruction}} - \underbrace{D_{KL}(q_\phi(\mathbf{z}\mid\mathbf{x})|p(\mathbf{z}))}_{\text{regularization}} \tag{23.5}$$

**Proof that the gap is the KL divergence:**

$$\log p_\theta(\mathbf{x}) - \mathcal{L}_{\text{ELBO}} = D_{KL}(q_\phi(\mathbf{z}\mid\mathbf{x})|p_\theta(\mathbf{z}\mid\mathbf{x})) \geq 0$$

**Proof:** $$\log p_\theta(\mathbf{x}) = \mathbb{E}_{q_\phi}!\left[\log p_\theta(\mathbf{x})\right] = \mathbb{E}_{q_\phi}!\left[\log\frac{p_\theta(\mathbf{x}\mid\mathbf{z})p(\mathbf{z})}{p_\theta(\mathbf{z}\mid\mathbf{x})}\right]$$ $$= \mathbb{E}_{q_\phi}!\left[\log\frac{p_\theta(\mathbf{x}\mid\mathbf{z})p(\mathbf{z})}{q_\phi(\mathbf{z}\mid\mathbf{x})}\right] + \mathbb{E}_{q_\phi}!\left[\log\frac{q_\phi(\mathbf{z}\mid\mathbf{x})}{p_\theta(\mathbf{z}\mid\mathbf{x})}\right]$$ $$= \mathcal{L}_{\text{ELBO}} + D_{KL}(q_\phi|p_\theta(\cdot\mid\mathbf{x})) \qquad \blacksquare$$

**Interpretation of ELBO terms:**

- **Reconstruction term** $\mathbb{E}_{q_\phi}[\log p_\theta(\mathbf{x}\mid\mathbf{z})]$: For Gaussian $p_\theta(\mathbf{x}\mid\mathbf{z}) = \mathcal{N}(\mu_\theta(\mathbf{z}), \sigma^2\mathbf{I})$, this equals $-|\mathbf{x}-\mu_\theta(\mathbf{z})|^2/2\sigma^2$ — the MSE reconstruction loss.
    
- **KL term** $D_{KL}(q_\phi|p)$: Regularizes the approximate posterior toward the prior. Forces the latent space to be structured — $q_\phi(\mathbf{z}\mid\mathbf{x})$ should not collapse to a deterministic encoder.
    

**Gaussian VAE — closed form KL:**

With $q_\phi(\mathbf{z}\mid\mathbf{x}) = \mathcal{N}(\boldsymbol\mu_\phi(\mathbf{x}), \text{diag}(\boldsymbol\sigma^2_\phi(\mathbf{x})))$ and $p(\mathbf{z}) = \mathcal{N}(\mathbf{0},\mathbf{I})$:

$$D_{KL}(q_\phi|p) = \frac{1}{2}\sum_{j=1}^{d_z}\left(\mu_{\phi,j}^2 + \sigma_{\phi,j}^2 - \log\sigma_{\phi,j}^2 - 1\right) \tag{23.6}$$

This closed form eliminates the need to estimate the KL by sampling.

**The Reparameterization Trick:**

The ELBO requires $\nabla_\phi\mathbb{E}_{q_\phi}[\log p_\theta(\mathbf{x}\mid\mathbf{z})]$ — but $\mathbf{z} \sim q_\phi(\mathbf{z}\mid\mathbf{x})$ depends on $\phi$, making naive Monte Carlo biased.

**Solution:** Write $\mathbf{z} = \boldsymbol\mu_\phi(\mathbf{x}) + \boldsymbol\sigma_\phi(\mathbf{x})\odot\boldsymbol\varepsilon$, $\boldsymbol\varepsilon\sim\mathcal{N}(\mathbf{0},\mathbf{I})$:

$$\mathbb{E}_{q_\phi(\mathbf{z}\mid\mathbf{x})}[f(\mathbf{z})] = \mathbb{E}_{\boldsymbol\varepsilon\sim\mathcal{N}(\mathbf{0},\mathbf{I})}!\left[f(\boldsymbol\mu_\phi(\mathbf{x}) + \boldsymbol\sigma_\phi(\mathbf{x})\odot\boldsymbol\varepsilon)\right] \tag{23.7}$$

Now $\boldsymbol\varepsilon$ is independent of $\phi$ — gradients flow through $\boldsymbol\mu_\phi$ and $\boldsymbol\sigma_\phi$ cleanly. $\blacksquare$

---

### 23.2.3 GANs — The Minimax Theorem

The GAN (Goodfellow et al., 2014) trains two networks adversarially:

- **Generator** $G_\theta: \mathcal{Z} \to \mathcal{X}$: maps noise $\mathbf{z}\sim p(\mathbf{z})$ to data space
- **Discriminator** $D_\phi: \mathcal{X} \to [0,1]$: classifies real ($D=1$) vs fake ($D=0$)

**The minimax objective:** $$\min_\theta\max_\phi,\mathcal{V}(\phi,\theta) = \mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{x}\sim p_{\text{data}}}!\left[\log D_\phi(\mathbf{x})\right] + \mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{z}\sim p(\mathbf{z})}!\left[\log(1-D_\phi(G_\theta(\mathbf{z})))\right] \tag{23.8}$$

**Theorem 23.1 (GAN Global Optimum — Goodfellow et al., 2014):**

_For fixed $G$, the optimal discriminator is:_ $$D^*(\mathbf{x}) = \frac{p_{\text{data}}(\mathbf{x})}{p_{\text{data}}(\mathbf{x}) + p_G(\mathbf{x})} \tag{23.9}$$

_where $p_G$ is the distribution of $G(\mathbf{z})$, $\mathbf{z}\sim p(\mathbf{z})$._

_The minimax value at $D^_$ reduces to:* $$C(G) = -\log 4 + 2,D_{JSD}(p_{\text{data}}|p_G) \tag{23.10}$$

_where $D_{JSD}$ is the Jensen-Shannon divergence:_ $$D_{JSD}(p|q) = \frac{1}{2}D_{KL}!\left(p,\Big|,\frac{p+q}{2}\right) + \frac{1}{2}D_{KL}!\left(q,\Big|,\frac{p+q}{2}\right) \tag{23.11}$$

_The global minimum $C(G^_) = -\log 4$ is achieved iff $p_G = p_{\text{data}}$.*

**Proof:**

For fixed $G$, $\mathcal{V}$ as a function of $D$ is: $$\mathcal{V} = \int!\left[p_{\text{data}}(\mathbf{x})\log D(\mathbf{x}) + p_G(\mathbf{x})\log(1-D(\mathbf{x}))\right]d\mathbf{x}$$

For each $\mathbf{x}$, maximize $a\log y + b\log(1-y)$ over $y\in(0,1)$: $$\frac{d}{dy}[a\log y + b\log(1-y)] = \frac{a}{y} - \frac{b}{1-y} = 0 \implies y^* = \frac{a}{a+b}$$

With $a = p_{\text{data}}(\mathbf{x})$, $b = p_G(\mathbf{x})$: $D^*(\mathbf{x}) = p_{\text{data}}(\mathbf{x})/(p_{\text{data}}(\mathbf{x})+p_G(\mathbf{x}))$. $\checkmark$

Substituting $D^*$ back: $$C(G) = \mathbb{E}_{p_{\text{data}}}!\left[\log\frac{p_{\text{data}}}{p_{\text{data}}+p_G}\right] + \mathbb{E}_{p_G}!\left[\log\frac{p_G}{p_{\text{data}}+p_G}\right]$$ $$= \mathbb{E}_{p_{\text{data}}}!\left[\log\frac{p_{\text{data}}}{(p_{\text{data}}+p_G)/2}\right] + \mathbb{E}_{p_G}!\left[\log\frac{p_G}{(p_{\text{data}}+p_G)/2}\right] - \log 4$$ $$= D_{KL}!\left(p_{\text{data}},\Big|,\frac{p_{\text{data}}+p_G}{2}\right) + D_{KL}!\left(p_G,\Big|,\frac{p_{\text{data}}+p_G}{2}\right) - \log 4$$ $$= 2,D_{JSD}(p_{\text{data}}|p_G) - \log 4 \geq -\log 4$$

Equality holds iff $D_{JSD} = 0 \iff p_G = p_{\text{data}}$. $\blacksquare$

**GAN training instabilities:**

Despite the elegant theory, GAN training suffers from:

- **Mode collapse:** The generator learns to produce only a subset of modes of $p_{\text{data}}$. Mathematically: the JSD is insensitive to the number of modes covered.
- **Vanishing gradients:** When $D$ is too good, $\log(1-D(G(\mathbf{z}))) \approx 0$ — gradient to $G$ vanishes.
- **Non-convergence:** The minimax game has no guaranteed Nash equilibrium in general.

**Wasserstein GAN (WGAN):** Replace JSD with the Wasserstein-1 distance: $$W_1(p_{\text{data}}, p_G) = \sup_{|f|_L\leq 1}\mathbb{E}_{p_{\text{data}}}[f(\mathbf{x})] - \mathbb{E}_{p_G}[f(G(\mathbf{z}))] \tag{23.12}$$

where the supremum is over 1-Lipschitz functions. The Wasserstein distance provides meaningful gradients even when $p_{\text{data}}$ and $p_G$ have disjoint supports — solving the vanishing gradient problem.

---

### 23.2.4 Score Matching and the Score Function

A key concept connecting all modern generative models is the **score function**:

$$\mathbf{s}_\theta(\mathbf{x}) = \nabla_\mathbf{x}\log p_\theta(\mathbf{x}) \tag{23.13}$$

The score function points in the direction of increasing log-probability — it is the gradient of the log-density with respect to the data point (not the parameters).

**Score matching objective** (Hyvärinen, 2005): We can estimate $\mathbf{s}_\theta$ without knowing $p_\theta(\mathbf{x})$:

$$\mathcal{L}_{\text{SM}} = \mathbb{E}_{p(\mathbf{x})}!\left[|\mathbf{s}_\theta(\mathbf{x}) - \nabla_\mathbf{x}\log p(\mathbf{x})|^2\right] \tag{23.14}$$

**Denoising score matching** (Vincent, 2011): For corrupted data $\tilde{\mathbf{x}} = \mathbf{x} + \sigma\boldsymbol\varepsilon$, $\boldsymbol\varepsilon\sim\mathcal{N}(\mathbf{0},\mathbf{I})$:

$$\mathcal{L}_{\text{DSM}}(\sigma) = \mathbb{E}_{p(\mathbf{x})}\mathbb{E}_{\boldsymbol\varepsilon}!\left[\left|\mathbf{s}_\theta(\tilde{\mathbf{x}}, \sigma) + \frac{\boldsymbol\varepsilon}{\sigma}\right|^2\right] \tag{23.15}$$

The optimal $\mathbf{s}_\theta^*(\tilde{\mathbf{x}},\sigma) = -\boldsymbol\varepsilon/\sigma$ is the normalized noise used to corrupt the data — the network learns to denoise.

---

### 23.2.5 Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models (DDPM)

Diffusion models (Ho et al., 2020) define a **forward noising process** and learn to reverse it. They achieve state-of-the-art image quality while maintaining tractable likelihood bounds.

**Forward process (fixed Markov chain adding noise):**

$$q(\mathbf{x}_t\mid\mathbf{x}_{t-1}) = \mathcal{N}(\mathbf{x}_t;\sqrt{1-\beta_t}\mathbf{x}_{t-1}, \beta_t\mathbf{I}) \tag{23.16}$$

The forward process gradually adds Gaussian noise. The key property: we can sample $\mathbf{x}_t$ directly from $\mathbf{x}_0$ in closed form:

$$q(\mathbf{x}_t\mid\mathbf{x}_0) = \mathcal{N}(\mathbf{x}_t;\sqrt{\bar\alpha_t},\mathbf{x}_0,,(1-\bar\alpha_t)\mathbf{I}) \tag{23.17}$$

where $\alpha_t = 1-\beta_t$ and $\bar\alpha_t = \prod_{s=1}^t\alpha_s$.

**Proof of Eq. 23.17:**

By induction: $\mathbf{x}_1 = \sqrt{\alpha_1}\mathbf{x}_0 + \sqrt{1-\alpha_1}\boldsymbol\varepsilon_1$. For $\mathbf{x}_2$: $$\mathbf{x}_2 = \sqrt{\alpha_2}\mathbf{x}_1 + \sqrt{1-\alpha_2}\boldsymbol\varepsilon_2 = \sqrt{\alpha_1\alpha_2}\mathbf{x}_0 + \sqrt{\alpha_2(1-\alpha_1)}\boldsymbol\varepsilon_1 + \sqrt{1-\alpha_2}\boldsymbol\varepsilon_2$$

Since $\sqrt{\alpha_2(1-\alpha_1)}\boldsymbol\varepsilon_1 + \sqrt{1-\alpha_2}\boldsymbol\varepsilon_2 \sim \mathcal{N}(\mathbf{0}, (1-\alpha_1\alpha_2)\mathbf{I})$ (sum of independent Gaussians): $$\mathbf{x}_2 = \sqrt{\bar\alpha_2}\mathbf{x}_0 + \sqrt{1-\bar\alpha_2}\boldsymbol\varepsilon, \quad \bar\alpha_2 = \alpha_1\alpha_2 \qquad \blacksquare$$

**The forward process reparameterization** (key for training): $$\mathbf{x}_t = \sqrt{\bar\alpha_t},\mathbf{x}_0 + \sqrt{1-\bar\alpha_t},\boldsymbol\varepsilon, \quad \boldsymbol\varepsilon\sim\mathcal{N}(\mathbf{0},\mathbf{I}) \tag{23.18}$$

**Reverse process (learned Markov chain):**

$$p_\theta(\mathbf{x}_{t-1}\mid\mathbf{x}_t) = \mathcal{N}(\mathbf{x}_{t-1};\boldsymbol\mu_\theta(\mathbf{x}_t, t),, \sigma_t^2\mathbf{I}) \tag{23.19}$$

The reverse process starts from pure noise $\mathbf{x}_T \sim \mathcal{N}(\mathbf{0},\mathbf{I})$ and iteratively denoises.

**DDPM training objective — the simplified noise prediction loss:**

> **Theorem 23.2 (DDPM ELBO Simplification):** The ELBO for the diffusion model simplifies to:
> 
> $$\mathcal{L}_{\text{simple}} = \mathbb{E}_{t, \mathbf{x}_0, \boldsymbol\varepsilon}!\left[|\boldsymbol\varepsilon - \boldsymbol\varepsilon_\theta(\mathbf{x}_t, t)|^2\right] \tag{23.20}$$
> 
> where $\boldsymbol\varepsilon_\theta(\mathbf{x}_t, t)$ is a neural network that predicts the noise added to $\mathbf{x}_0$.

**Proof sketch:**

The full ELBO for a diffusion model is: $$\mathcal{L} = \mathbb{E}_q!\left[\log p_\theta(\mathbf{x}_0\mid\mathbf{x}_1) - \sum_{t=2}^T D_{KL}(q(\mathbf{x}_{t-1}\mid\mathbf{x}_t,\mathbf{x}_0)|p_\theta(\mathbf{x}_{t-1}\mid\mathbf{x}_t))\right]$$

The posterior $q(\mathbf{x}_{t-1}\mid\mathbf{x}_t, \mathbf{x}_0)$ is tractable (Gaussian by Bayes' theorem on Gaussians): $$q(\mathbf{x}_{t-1}\mid\mathbf{x}_t,\mathbf{x}_0) = \mathcal{N}(\tilde{\boldsymbol\mu}_t(\mathbf{x}_t,\mathbf{x}_0), \tilde\beta_t\mathbf{I}) \tag{23.21}$$

$$\tilde{\boldsymbol\mu}_t = \frac{\sqrt{\bar\alpha_{t-1}}\beta_t}{1-\bar\alpha_t}\mathbf{x}_0 + \frac{\sqrt{\alpha_t}(1-\bar\alpha_{t-1})}{1-\bar\alpha_t}\mathbf{x}_t \tag{23.22}$$

The KL between two Gaussians with equal variance is $\propto |\tilde{\boldsymbol\mu}_t - \boldsymbol\mu_\theta|^2$.

Setting $\boldsymbol\mu_\theta(\mathbf{x}_t,t) = \frac{1}{\sqrt{\alpha_t}}!\left(\mathbf{x}_t - \frac{\beta_t}{\sqrt{1-\bar\alpha_t}}\boldsymbol\varepsilon_\theta(\mathbf{x}_t,t)\right)$ and substituting $\mathbf{x}_0$ via (23.18), the KL simplifies to $|\boldsymbol\varepsilon - \boldsymbol\varepsilon_\theta(\mathbf{x}_t,t)|^2$. $\blacksquare$

**DDPM sampling (reverse diffusion):**

$$\mathbf{x}_{t-1} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{\alpha_t}}!\left(\mathbf{x}_t - \frac{\beta_t}{\sqrt{1-\bar\alpha_t}}\boldsymbol\varepsilon_\theta(\mathbf{x}_t, t)\right) + \sqrt{\beta_t},\mathbf{z}, \quad \mathbf{z}\sim\mathcal{N}(\mathbf{0},\mathbf{I}) \tag{23.23}$$

Requires $T$ (typically 1000) neural network forward passes for one sample — the main computational cost.

**Score function connection:** The denoising network implicitly estimates the score: $$\boldsymbol\varepsilon_\theta(\mathbf{x}_t, t) \approx -\sqrt{1-\bar\alpha_t}\nabla_{\mathbf{x}_t}\log p(\mathbf{x}_t) \tag{23.24}$$

This connects DDPM directly to score matching — diffusion models are score matching at multiple noise scales simultaneously.

---

### 23.2.6 Noise Schedule

The noise schedule ${\beta_t}_{t=1}^T$ controls the forward process. Key constraints:

- $\bar\alpha_T \approx 0$ so $\mathbf{x}_T \approx \mathcal{N}(\mathbf{0},\mathbf{I})$ (pure noise)
- $\bar\alpha_0 = 1$ so $\mathbf{x}_0 = \mathbf{x}$ (no noise)

**Linear schedule** (original DDPM): $\beta_t$ increases linearly from $\beta_1 = 10^{-4}$ to $\beta_T = 0.02$.

**Cosine schedule** (Nichol & Dhariwal, 2021): $$\bar\alpha_t = \cos^2!\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\cdot\frac{t/T + s}{1+s}\right) \bigg/ \cos^2!\left(\frac{\pi s}{2(1+s)}\right) \tag{23.25}$$

The cosine schedule provides more noise at small $t$ and less at large $t$, improving performance on tasks requiring fine detail.

---

### 23.2.7 Comparison of Generative Models

|Property|AE|VAE|GAN|Diffusion|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Sample quality|N/A|Blurry|Sharp|Excellent|
|Likelihood|No|Lower bound (ELBO)|No (implicit)|Lower bound|
|Training stability|High|High|Low|High|
|Sampling speed|Fast|Fast|Fast|Slow ($T$ steps)|
|Mode coverage|N/A|Moderate|Low (collapse)|High|
|Latent space|Yes|Structured|No|No|
|Objective|MSE recon.|ELBO (Eq. 23.5)|Minimax (Eq. 23.8)|Noise pred. (Eq. 23.20)|

## 23.3 Numerical Examples

### Example 23.1: ELBO Computation

**VAE with** $d_z=2$. Encoder outputs: $\boldsymbol\mu = (0.5, -0.3)$, $\log\boldsymbol\sigma^2 = (-0.4, 0.2)$. Reconstruction MSE: 0.23 per pixel for a 32×32 image.

**KL divergence** (Eq. 23.6): $$D_{KL} = \frac{1}{2}!\left[(0.5^2 + e^{-0.4} - (-0.4) - 1) + ((-0.3)^2 + e^{0.2} - 0.2 - 1)\right]$$ $$= \frac{1}{2}[(0.25 + 0.670 + 0.4 - 1) + (0.09 + 1.221 - 0.2 - 1)] = \frac{1}{2}[0.320 + 0.111] = 0.216$$

**Reconstruction term:** For $32\times32\times3 = 3072$ pixels with Gaussian $p_\theta(\mathbf{x}\mid\mathbf{z})$, $\sigma=1$: $$\mathbb{E}[\log p_\theta(\mathbf{x}\mid\mathbf{z})] = -\frac{3072}{2}(\log 2\pi + 0.23) \approx -4097$$

**ELBO** $= -4097 - 0.216 = -4097.2$ (dominated by reconstruction). In practice, a weighting $\beta$ multiplies the KL term to balance the two objectives ($\beta$-VAE).

---

### Example 23.2: DDPM Forward Process

**Image** $\mathbf{x}_0 \in \mathbb{R}^{1024}$ (32×32 grayscale). Linear schedule: $T=1000$, $\beta_t = 0.0001 + 0.0199\cdot(t-1)/999$.

At $t=250$: $\bar\alpha_{250} = \prod_{s=1}^{250}(1-\beta_s)$. With linear $\beta$: $\bar\alpha_{250} \approx e^{-\sum\beta} \approx e^{-0.53} \approx 0.589$.

$\mathbf{x}_{250} = \sqrt{0.589}\mathbf{x}_0 + \sqrt{0.411}\boldsymbol\varepsilon \approx 0.768\mathbf{x}_0 + 0.641\boldsymbol\varepsilon$

Signal-to-noise ratio: $\text{SNR}(250) = \bar\alpha_{250}/(1-\bar\alpha_{250}) = 0.589/0.411 = 1.43$ — still mostly signal.

At $t=800$: $\bar\alpha_{800} \approx 0.034$. $\text{SNR}(800) = 0.034/0.966 = 0.035$ — mostly noise. The image is nearly unrecognizable.

At $t=1000$: $\bar\alpha_{1000} \approx 0$ — pure Gaussian noise. Sampling begins here.

---

## 23.4 Implementation

```python
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.gridspec as gridspec
from typing import Optional, Tuple, List, Dict, Callable

# =============================================================================
# MODULE 23: GENERATIVE MODELS
# =============================================================================

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# PART A: Autoencoder
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

class Autoencoder:
    """
    Deterministic Autoencoder. Eq. 23.1.
    Encoder: d_x → d_h → d_z (bottleneck)
    Decoder: d_z → d_h → d_x
    """

    def __init__(self, d_x: int, d_z: int, d_h: int = 128, seed: int = 42):
        rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
        std = lambda d_in: np.sqrt(2/d_in)

        # Encoder weights
        self.We1 = rng.normal(0, std(d_x), (d_h, d_x))
        self.be1 = np.zeros(d_h)
        self.We2 = rng.normal(0, std(d_h), (d_z, d_h))
        self.be2 = np.zeros(d_z)

        # Decoder weights
        self.Wd1 = rng.normal(0, std(d_z), (d_h, d_z))
        self.bd1 = np.zeros(d_h)
        self.Wd2 = rng.normal(0, std(d_h), (d_x, d_h))
        self.bd2 = np.zeros(d_x)

        self.cache = {}

    @staticmethod
    def _relu(z): return np.maximum(0, z)
    @staticmethod
    def _relu_grad(z): return (z > 0).astype(float)

    def encode(self, X: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
        """Encoder: X → z (deterministic)"""
        h1 = self._relu(X @ self.We1.T + self.be1)
        z  = X @ self.We1.T + self.be1   # pre-act
        h1 = self._relu(z)
        z2 = h1 @ self.We2.T + self.be2
        self.cache['encode'] = {'X': X, 'h1': h1, 'z1': z, 'z2': z2}
        return z2

    def decode(self, z: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
        """Decoder: z → X_hat"""
        h  = self._relu(z @ self.Wd1.T + self.bd1)
        xh = h @ self.Wd2.T + self.bd2   # linear output
        self.cache['decode'] = {'z': z, 'h': h}
        return xh

    def forward(self, X: np.ndarray) -> Tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
        z    = self.encode(X)
        xhat = self.decode(z)
        return xhat, z

    def loss(self, X: np.ndarray) -> float:
        """MSE reconstruction loss. Eq. 23.1."""
        xhat, _ = self.forward(X)
        return float(np.mean((X - xhat)**2))


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# PART B: Variational Autoencoder (VAE)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

class VAE:
    """
    Variational Autoencoder. Eqs. 23.3-23.7.
    Encoder: q_phi(z|x) = N(mu, diag(sigma^2))
    Decoder: p_theta(x|z) = N(mu_theta(z), I)
    Training: maximize ELBO = E[log p(x|z)] - KL(q||p)
    """

    def __init__(self, d_x: int, d_z: int, d_h: int = 128,
                  beta: float = 1.0, seed: int = 42):
        """
        beta: weight on KL term (beta=1: standard VAE, beta>1: beta-VAE)
        """
        rng  = np.random.default_rng(seed)
        std  = lambda d: np.sqrt(2/d)
        self.d_x = d_x; self.d_z = d_z; self.beta = beta

        # Encoder (shared hidden layer, two output heads)
        self.We1   = rng.normal(0, std(d_x), (d_h, d_x))
        self.be1   = np.zeros(d_h)
        self.Wmu   = rng.normal(0, std(d_h), (d_z, d_h))
        self.bmu   = np.zeros(d_z)
        self.Wlog  = rng.normal(0, std(d_h), (d_z, d_h))
        self.blog  = np.zeros(d_z)   # log sigma^2

        # Decoder
        self.Wd1   = rng.normal(0, std(d_z), (d_h, d_z))
        self.bd1   = np.zeros(d_h)
        self.Wd2   = rng.normal(0, std(d_h), (d_x, d_h))
        self.bd2   = np.zeros(d_x)

        # Adam optimizer state
        self._init_adam()

    def _init_adam(self):
        self._m = {}; self._v = {}; self._t = 0
        for name in ['We1','be1','Wmu','bmu','Wlog','blog','Wd1','bd1','Wd2','bd2']:
            p = getattr(self, name)
            self._m[name] = np.zeros_like(p)
            self._v[name] = np.zeros_like(p)

    @staticmethod
    def _relu(z): return np.maximum(0, z)
    @staticmethod
    def _relu_g(z): return (z > 0).astype(float)

    def encode(self, X: np.ndarray, seed: int = None
               ) -> Tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
        """
        Encoder forward pass. Returns (mu, log_var, z_sample).
        z = mu + sigma * epsilon  [reparameterization trick, Eq. 23.7]
        """
        rng    = np.random.default_rng(seed)
        h1_pre = X @ self.We1.T + self.be1
        h1     = self._relu(h1_pre)
        mu     = h1 @ self.Wmu.T  + self.bmu      # mean of q(z|x)
        log_var= h1 @ self.Wlog.T + self.blog      # log variance of q(z|x)

        # Reparameterization trick (Eq. 23.7)
        eps    = rng.standard_normal(mu.shape)
        sigma  = np.exp(0.5 * log_var)
        z      = mu + sigma * eps                  # z ~ q(z|x) via reparameterization

        self._enc_cache = {'X': X, 'h1_pre': h1_pre, 'h1': h1,
                            'mu': mu, 'log_var': log_var,
                            'sigma': sigma, 'eps': eps, 'z': z}
        return mu, log_var, z

    def decode(self, z: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
        """Decoder forward pass. Returns reconstructed x."""
        h_pre = z @ self.Wd1.T + self.bd1
        h     = self._relu(h_pre)
        x_hat = h @ self.Wd2.T + self.bd2   # linear: N(x_hat, I)
        self._dec_cache = {'z': z, 'h_pre': h_pre, 'h': h, 'x_hat': x_hat}
        return x_hat

    def elbo(self, X: np.ndarray, seed: int = None) -> Tuple[float, float, float]:
        """
        Compute ELBO = E[log p(x|z)] - beta * KL(q||p). Eq. 23.5.
        Returns (elbo, recon_loss, kl_loss).
        """
        mu, log_var, z = self.encode(X, seed=seed)
        x_hat = self.decode(z)

        # Reconstruction: E[log p(x|z)] for Gaussian = -||x - x_hat||^2 / 2
        recon = -0.5 * np.mean(np.sum((X - x_hat)**2, axis=1))

        # KL divergence (closed form, Eq. 23.6)
        kl = 0.5 * np.mean(np.sum(mu**2 + np.exp(log_var) - log_var - 1, axis=1))

        elbo_val = recon - self.beta * kl
        return float(elbo_val), float(-recon), float(kl)

    def step(self, X: np.ndarray, lr: float = 1e-3, seed: int = None):
        """
        One training step: compute ELBO gradients, update with Adam.
        """
        mu, log_var, z = self.encode(X, seed=seed)
        x_hat = self.decode(z)
        sigma  = self._enc_cache['sigma']
        eps    = self._enc_cache['eps']
        h1     = self._enc_cache['h1']
        h1_pre = self._enc_cache['h1_pre']

        n = len(X)
        # === Decoder gradients ===
        dL_dxhat = -(X - x_hat) / n      # gradient of reconstruction loss
        h_dec = self._dec_cache['h']
        h_dec_pre = self._dec_cache['h_pre']

        dWd2 = dL_dxhat.T @ h_dec
        dbd2 = dL_dxhat.sum(axis=0)
        dh   = dL_dxhat @ self.Wd2
        dh_pre = dh * self._relu_g(h_dec_pre)
        dWd1 = dh_pre.T @ z
        dbd1 = dh_pre.sum(axis=0)
        dz   = dh_pre @ self.Wd1          # gradient w.r.t. z

        # === Encoder gradients (via reparameterization, Eq. 23.7) ===
        # KL gradients w.r.t. mu and log_var (Eq. 23.6 differentiated)
        dkl_dmu    = self.beta * mu / n
        dkl_dlogv  = self.beta * 0.5 * (np.exp(log_var) - 1) / n

        # z = mu + sigma*eps  →  dL/dmu, dL/dlog_var via chain rule
        dmu    = dz + dkl_dmu
        dsigma = dz * eps
        dlogv  = dsigma * sigma * 0.5 + dkl_dlogv   # d(sigma)/d(log_var/2) = sigma/2

        dWmu  = dmu.T  @ h1
        dbmu  = dmu.sum(axis=0)
        dWlog = dlogv.T @ h1
        dblog = dlogv.sum(axis=0)

        dh1   = dmu @ self.Wmu + dlogv @ self.Wlog
        dh1_pre = dh1 * self._relu_g(h1_pre)
        dWe1  = dh1_pre.T @ X
        dbe1  = dh1_pre.sum(axis=0)

        # Adam update
        self._t += 1
        grads = {'We1': dWe1, 'be1': dbe1, 'Wmu': dWmu, 'bmu': dbmu,
                  'Wlog': dWlog, 'blog': dblog, 'Wd1': dWd1, 'bd1': dbd1,
                  'Wd2': dWd2, 'bd2': dbd2}
        b1, b2, eps_adam = 0.9, 0.999, 1e-8
        for name, g in grads.items():
            self._m[name] = b1*self._m[name] + (1-b1)*g
            self._v[name] = b2*self._v[name] + (1-b2)*g**2
            mhat = self._m[name]/(1-b1**self._t)
            vhat = self._v[name]/(1-b2**self._t)
            setattr(self, name, getattr(self, name) - lr*mhat/(np.sqrt(vhat)+eps_adam))

    def sample(self, n: int = 16, seed: int = 42) -> np.ndarray:
        """Sample from the prior p(z) and decode. Eq. 23.3."""
        rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
        z   = rng.standard_normal((n, self.d_z))
        return self.decode(z)

    def fit(self, X: np.ndarray, n_epochs: int = 100,
             lr: float = 1e-3, batch_size: int = 64,
             seed: int = 42) -> Dict:
        """Training loop."""
        rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
        n   = len(X)
        history = {'elbo': [], 'recon': [], 'kl': []}

        for epoch in range(n_epochs):
            idx = rng.permutation(n)
            epoch_elbo = epoch_recon = epoch_kl = 0.0
            n_batches  = 0

            for start in range(0, n, batch_size):
                Xb   = X[idx[start:start+batch_size]]
                self.step(Xb, lr=lr, seed=int(epoch*1000+n_batches))
                elbo, recon, kl = self.elbo(Xb, seed=int(epoch*1000+n_batches))
                epoch_elbo  += elbo; epoch_recon += recon; epoch_kl += kl
                n_batches   += 1

            history['elbo'].append(epoch_elbo/n_batches)
            history['recon'].append(epoch_recon/n_batches)
            history['kl'].append(epoch_kl/n_batches)

        return history


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# PART C: GAN
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

class GAN:
    """
    Generative Adversarial Network. Eqs. 23.8-23.11.
    Simple MLP generator and discriminator.
    """

    def __init__(self, d_x: int, d_z: int = 16, d_h: int = 64, seed: int = 42):
        rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
        std = lambda d: np.sqrt(2/d)
        self.d_z = d_z

        # Generator: z -> x (MLP)
        self.Wg1 = rng.normal(0, std(d_z), (d_h, d_z))
        self.bg1 = np.zeros(d_h)
        self.Wg2 = rng.normal(0, std(d_h), (d_x, d_h))
        self.bg2 = np.zeros(d_x)

        # Discriminator: x -> [0,1] (MLP)
        self.Wd1 = rng.normal(0, std(d_x), (d_h, d_x))
        self.bdd1 = np.zeros(d_h)
        self.Wd2 = rng.normal(0, std(d_h), (1, d_h))
        self.bdd2 = np.zeros(1)

    @staticmethod
    def _sigmoid(z): return 1/(1+np.exp(-np.clip(z,-500,500)))
    @staticmethod
    def _relu(z): return np.maximum(0, z)
    @staticmethod
    def _relu_g(z): return (z > 0).astype(float)

    def generate(self, z: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
        """Generator forward pass. G(z) = decode(z)."""
        h   = self._relu(z @ self.Wg1.T + self.bg1)
        x   = h @ self.Wg2.T + self.bg2   # linear output
        self._g_cache = {'z': z, 'h': h}
        return x

    def discriminate(self, x: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
        """Discriminator forward pass. D(x) -> probability of real."""
        h   = self._relu(x @ self.Wd1.T + self.bdd1)
        logit = h @ self.Wd2.T + self.bdd2
        self._d_cache = {'x': x, 'h': h, 'logit': logit}
        return self._sigmoid(logit)

    def discriminator_loss(self, x_real: np.ndarray,
                            x_fake: np.ndarray) -> float:
        """
        Discriminator loss: Eq. 23.8, maximize over D.
        L_D = E[log D(x_real)] + E[log(1 - D(x_fake))]
        """
        d_real = self.discriminate(x_real)
        d_fake = self.discriminate(x_fake)
        loss   = -(np.log(d_real + 1e-12) + np.log(1 - d_fake + 1e-12)).mean()
        return float(loss)

    def generator_loss(self, z: np.ndarray) -> float:
        """
        Generator loss: minimize log(1-D(G(z))) ≡ maximize log D(G(z)).
        The non-saturating version for better gradients.
        """
        x_fake = self.generate(z)
        d_fake = self.discriminate(x_fake)
        # Non-saturating: -log D(G(z)) instead of log(1-D(G(z)))
        loss   = -np.log(d_fake + 1e-12).mean()
        return float(loss)

    def optimal_discriminator(self, x: np.ndarray,
                               p_data: np.ndarray,
                               p_gen: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
        """
        Compute optimal discriminator D*(x). Eq. 23.9.
        D*(x) = p_data(x) / (p_data(x) + p_G(x))
        """
        return p_data / (p_data + p_gen + 1e-12)

    def jsd(self, p: np.ndarray, q: np.ndarray) -> float:
        """Jensen-Shannon divergence. Eq. 23.11."""
        m   = (p + q) / 2
        kl_pm = np.sum(p * np.log(p / (m + 1e-12) + 1e-12))
        kl_qm = np.sum(q * np.log(q / (m + 1e-12) + 1e-12))
        return float(0.5 * kl_pm + 0.5 * kl_qm)

    def train_step(self, x_real: np.ndarray, lr_d: float = 1e-4,
                    lr_g: float = 1e-4, seed: int = 42) -> Tuple[float, float]:
        """One GAN training step: update D then G."""
        rng    = np.random.default_rng(seed)
        n      = len(x_real)
        z      = rng.standard_normal((n, self.d_z))
        x_fake = self.generate(z)

        # ---- Discriminator step ----
        d_real = self.discriminate(x_real)
        d_fake_detached = self.discriminate(x_fake.copy())

        # Gradients for discriminator
        dL_dlogit_real = -(1/(d_real + 1e-12)) * d_real * (1-d_real) / n
        dL_dlogit_fake = (1/(1-d_fake_detached+1e-12)) * d_fake_detached * (1-d_fake_detached) / n

        h_r  = self._d_cache['h']
        dWd2 = (dL_dlogit_real.T @ h_r + dL_dlogit_fake.T @ self._d_cache['h'])
        dbd2 = (dL_dlogit_real + dL_dlogit_fake).sum(axis=0)
        dh_r = dL_dlogit_real @ self.Wd2; dh_r_pre = dh_r * self._relu_g(x_real@self.Wd1.T+self.bdd1)
        dh_f = dL_dlogit_fake @ self.Wd2; dh_f_pre = dh_f * self._relu_g(x_fake@self.Wd1.T+self.bdd1)
        dWd1 = dh_r_pre.T @ x_real + dh_f_pre.T @ x_fake
        dbd1 = (dh_r_pre + dh_f_pre).sum(axis=0)

        self.Wd2  -= lr_d * dWd2; self.bdd2 -= lr_d * dbd2
        self.Wd1  -= lr_d * dWd1; self.bdd1 -= lr_d * dbd1

        # ---- Generator step ----
        z      = rng.standard_normal((n, self.d_z))
        x_fake = self.generate(z)
        d_fake = self.discriminate(x_fake)

        dL_dlogit_g = -(1/(d_fake+1e-12)) * d_fake * (1-d_fake) / n
        dL_dx_fake  = (dL_dlogit_g @ self.Wd2) * self._relu_g(x_fake@self.Wd1.T+self.bdd1) @ self.Wd1

        h_g    = self._g_cache['h']
        dWg2   = dL_dx_fake.T @ h_g
        dbg2   = dL_dx_fake.sum(axis=0)
        dh_g   = dL_dx_fake @ self.Wg2
        dh_gpre= dh_g * self._relu_g(z @ self.Wg1.T + self.bg1)
        dWg1   = dh_gpre.T @ z
        dbg1   = dh_gpre.sum(axis=0)

        self.Wg2 -= lr_g * dWg2; self.bg2 -= lr_g * dbg2
        self.Wg1 -= lr_g * dWg1; self.bg1 -= lr_g * dbg1

        d_loss = self.discriminator_loss(x_real, x_fake)
        g_loss = self.generator_loss(rng.standard_normal((n, self.d_z)))
        return d_loss, g_loss


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# PART D: DDPM (Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Model)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

class DDPM:
    """
    Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Model. Eqs. 23.16-23.23.
    Uses a simple MLP denoising network for pedagogical clarity.
    In practice: U-Net architecture with sinusoidal time embeddings.
    """

    def __init__(self, d_x: int, d_h: int = 256, T: int = 200,
                  schedule: str = 'linear', seed: int = 42):
        rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
        self.T   = T
        self.d_x = d_x

        # Noise schedule
        self.betas     = self._make_schedule(T, schedule)
        self.alphas    = 1 - self.betas
        self.alpha_bar = np.cumprod(self.alphas)              # bar alpha_t
        self.sqrt_abar      = np.sqrt(self.alpha_bar)
        self.sqrt_one_mabar = np.sqrt(1 - self.alpha_bar)

        # Denoising network: (x_t, t_embed) → epsilon_hat
        # Input: d_x + T (one-hot time) → d_h → d_h → d_x
        std = lambda d: np.sqrt(2/d)
        d_in = d_x + 32   # time embedding dimension = 32
        self.W1 = rng.normal(0, std(d_in), (d_h, d_in))
        self.b1 = np.zeros(d_h)
        self.W2 = rng.normal(0, std(d_h), (d_h, d_h))
        self.b2 = np.zeros(d_h)
        self.W3 = rng.normal(0, std(d_h), (d_x, d_h))
        self.b3 = np.zeros(d_x)

        # Time embedding
        self.t_embed = self._sinusoidal_embedding(T, 32)

        # Adam state
        self._m = {k: np.zeros_like(v) for k,v in
                    [('W1',self.W1),('b1',self.b1),('W2',self.W2),
                     ('b2',self.b2),('W3',self.W3),('b3',self.b3)]}
        self._v = {k: np.zeros_like(v) for k in self._m}
        self._t_adam = 0

    @staticmethod
    def _sinusoidal_embedding(T: int, d: int) -> np.ndarray:
        """Sinusoidal time embeddings (same principle as PE, Eqs. 22.9-22.10)."""
        pos  = np.arange(T)[:, None]
        freq = 1 / (10000 ** (2*np.arange(d//2)[None,:] / d))
        emb  = np.zeros((T, d))
        emb[:, 0::2] = np.sin(pos * freq)
        emb[:, 1::2] = np.cos(pos * freq)
        return emb

    @staticmethod
    def _make_schedule(T: int, schedule: str) -> np.ndarray:
        if schedule == 'linear':
            return np.linspace(1e-4, 0.02, T)
        elif schedule == 'cosine':
            s = 0.008
            t = np.arange(T+1)
            f = np.cos(((t/T + s)/(1+s)) * np.pi/2)**2
            f = f / f[0]
            betas = np.clip(1 - f[1:]/f[:-1], 0, 0.999)
            return betas
        else:
            raise ValueError(f"Unknown schedule: {schedule}")

    def q_sample(self, x0: np.ndarray, t: np.ndarray,
                  eps: Optional[np.ndarray] = None,
                  seed: int = 42) -> Tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
        """
        Sample x_t from x_0 using the closed-form forward process. Eq. 23.18.
        x_t = sqrt(alpha_bar_t) * x_0 + sqrt(1-alpha_bar_t) * eps
        """
        if eps is None:
            eps = np.random.default_rng(seed).standard_normal(x0.shape)
        sqrt_ab   = self.sqrt_abar[t][:, None]      # (batch, 1)
        sqrt_1mab = self.sqrt_one_mabar[t][:, None]
        x_t       = sqrt_ab * x0 + sqrt_1mab * eps  # Eq. 23.18
        return x_t, eps

    def denoise_net(self, x_t: np.ndarray, t: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
        """
        Denoising network: eps_theta(x_t, t). Predicts the noise.
        x_t: (batch, d_x), t: (batch,) int
        """
        t_emb = self.t_embed[t]                              # (batch, 32)
        inp   = np.concatenate([x_t, t_emb], axis=1)        # (batch, d_x+32)
        h1    = np.maximum(0, inp @ self.W1.T + self.b1)
        h2    = np.maximum(0, h1  @ self.W2.T + self.b2)
        eps_hat = h2 @ self.W3.T + self.b3
        self._dn_cache = {'inp': inp, 'h1': h1, 'h2': h2, 'x_t': x_t, 't': t}
        return eps_hat

    def training_loss(self, x0: np.ndarray, seed: int = 42) -> float:
        """
        DDPM training loss. Eq. 23.20: E[||eps - eps_theta(x_t, t)||^2]
        Sample t uniformly, corrupt x0, predict noise.
        """
        rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
        n   = len(x0)
        t   = rng.integers(0, self.T, n)          # sample timesteps
        eps = rng.standard_normal(x0.shape)        # sample noise
        x_t, eps = self.q_sample(x0, t, eps)
        eps_hat  = self.denoise_net(x_t, t)
        return float(np.mean((eps - eps_hat)**2))  # Eq. 23.20

    def train_step(self, x0: np.ndarray, lr: float = 1e-3, seed: int = 42):
        """One training step with Adam optimizer."""
        rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
        n   = len(x0)
        t   = rng.integers(0, self.T, n)
        eps = rng.standard_normal(x0.shape)
        x_t, eps = self.q_sample(x0, t, eps)

        eps_hat = self.denoise_net(x_t, t)
        cache   = self._dn_cache

        # Gradients (MSE loss)
        dL = 2*(eps_hat - eps)/n
        dW3 = dL.T @ cache['h2']
        db3 = dL.sum(axis=0)
        dh2 = dL @ self.W3
        dh2_pre = dh2 * (cache['h2'] > 0)
        dW2 = dh2_pre.T @ cache['h1']
        db2 = dh2_pre.sum(axis=0)
        dh1 = dh2_pre @ self.W2
        dh1_pre = dh1 * (cache['h1'] > 0)
        dW1 = dh1_pre.T @ cache['inp']
        db1 = dh1_pre.sum(axis=0)

        # Adam update
        self._t_adam += 1
        b1, b2, ep = 0.9, 0.999, 1e-8
        for name, g in [('W1',dW1),('b1',db1),('W2',dW2),
                          ('b2',db2),('W3',dW3),('b3',db3)]:
            self._m[name] = b1*self._m[name] + (1-b1)*g
            self._v[name] = b2*self._v[name] + (1-b2)*g**2
            mh = self._m[name]/(1-b1**self._t_adam)
            vh = self._v[name]/(1-b2**self._t_adam)
            setattr(self, name, getattr(self, name) - lr*mh/(np.sqrt(vh)+ep))

    def sample(self, n: int = 16, seed: int = 42) -> np.ndarray:
        """
        DDPM sampling (reverse diffusion). Eq. 23.23.
        Start from x_T ~ N(0,I), iteratively denoise.
        """
        rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
        x   = rng.standard_normal((n, self.d_x))   # x_T ~ N(0,I)

        for t_idx in reversed(range(self.T)):
            t_arr = np.full(n, t_idx, dtype=int)
            eps_hat = self.denoise_net(x, t_arr)

            # Reverse step (Eq. 23.23)
            alpha_t   = self.alphas[t_idx]
            abar_t    = self.alpha_bar[t_idx]
            beta_t    = self.betas[t_idx]

            # Predicted mean
            mu = (1/np.sqrt(alpha_t)) * (
                x - (beta_t/np.sqrt(1-abar_t)) * eps_hat)

            if t_idx > 0:
                sigma = np.sqrt(beta_t)
                z     = rng.standard_normal(x.shape)
                x     = mu + sigma * z    # add noise (for t>0)
            else:
                x     = mu               # final step: no noise

        return x

    def fit(self, X: np.ndarray, n_epochs: int = 50,
             lr: float = 1e-3, batch_size: int = 64,
             seed: int = 42) -> List[float]:
        """Training loop."""
        rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
        n   = len(X)
        losses = []

        for epoch in range(n_epochs):
            idx = rng.permutation(n)
            epoch_loss = 0.0; n_batches = 0

            for start in range(0, n, batch_size):
                Xb = X[idx[start:start+batch_size]]
                self.train_step(Xb, lr=lr, seed=epoch*1000+n_batches)
                epoch_loss += self.training_loss(Xb, seed=epoch*1000+n_batches)
                n_batches  += 1

            losses.append(epoch_loss/n_batches)

        return losses


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# PART E: Comprehensive Visualization
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

def full_visualization(seed: int = 42):
    """
    Full visualization: latent space, ELBO, GAN theory, diffusion process.
    """
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    fig = plt.figure(figsize=(18, 14))
    gs  = gridspec.GridSpec(3, 4, wspace=0.38, hspace=0.48)

    # ---- 1: ELBO decomposition ----
    ax = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, 0])
    beta_vals = np.logspace(-2, 1, 100)
    # Simulate ELBO components as function of beta
    recon_base = 50.0
    kl_base    = 5.0
    # As beta increases: KL decreases (more regularized z), recon increases
    kl_vals    = kl_base / (1 + 0.3*beta_vals)
    recon_vals = recon_base + 10*np.log(1 + 0.5*beta_vals)
    elbo_vals  = -(recon_vals + beta_vals * kl_vals)

    ax.semilogx(beta_vals, recon_vals, '#e84040', lw=2.5, label='Recon loss -E[log p(x|z)]')
    ax.semilogx(beta_vals, beta_vals*kl_vals, '#1a6faf', lw=2.5, linestyle='--',
                label='β·KL(q||p)')
    ax.semilogx(beta_vals, -elbo_vals, '#2ca02c', lw=2.5, linestyle=':',
                label='Total loss (-ELBO)')
    ax.axvline(1.0, color='gray', lw=1.5, linestyle='--', alpha=0.7, label='β=1 (standard VAE)')
    ax.set_xlabel("β (KL weight)"); ax.set_ylabel("Loss")
    ax.set_title("ELBO Components (Eq. 23.5)\nβ-VAE tradeoff",
                 fontsize=10, fontweight='bold')
    ax.legend(fontsize=7); ax.grid(alpha=0.3, which='both')

    # ---- 2: Reparameterization trick ----
    ax = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, 1])
    mu_vals = np.linspace(-2, 2, 200)
    sig_vals = np.linspace(0.1, 2, 200)
    eps_fixed = rng.standard_normal(1000)
    # Show that z = mu + sigma*eps is differentiable in mu, sigma
    mu = 0.5; sigma = 1.2
    z_samples = mu + sigma * eps_fixed
    ax.hist(z_samples, bins=40, density=True, alpha=0.6, color='#1a6faf',
            label=f'z ~ q(z|x), μ={mu}, σ={sigma}')
    z_range = np.linspace(-4, 5, 300)
    ax.plot(z_range, np.exp(-0.5*(z_range-mu)**2/sigma**2)/(sigma*np.sqrt(2*np.pi)),
            '#e84040', lw=2.5, label='N(μ, σ²)')
    ax.plot(z_range, np.exp(-0.5*z_range**2)/np.sqrt(2*np.pi),
            'k--', lw=1.5, alpha=0.6, label='Prior N(0,1)')
    ax.set_title("Reparameterization Trick (Eq. 23.7)\nz = μ + σ·ε, ε~N(0,I)",
                 fontsize=10, fontweight='bold')
    ax.legend(fontsize=8); ax.grid(alpha=0.3)

    # ---- 3: GAN optimal discriminator ----
    ax = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, 2])
    x_range = np.linspace(-4, 4, 300)
    p_data = np.exp(-0.5*(x_range-1)**2) / np.sqrt(2*np.pi)
    p_gen  = np.exp(-0.5*(x_range+0.5)**2*0.5) * np.sqrt(0.5/np.pi)
    D_opt  = p_data / (p_data + p_gen + 1e-12)

    ax.plot(x_range, p_data, '#1a6faf', lw=2.5, label='p_data(x)')
    ax.plot(x_range, p_gen,  '#e84040', lw=2.5, linestyle='--', label='p_G(x)')
    ax.plot(x_range, D_opt,  '#2ca02c', lw=2.5, linestyle=':',
            label='D*(x) = p_data/(p_data+p_G)')
    ax.axhline(0.5, color='gray', lw=1, linestyle='--', alpha=0.5,
               label='D=0.5 (optimal at p_G=p_data)')
    ax.set_title("GAN Optimal Discriminator (Eq. 23.9)\nTheorem 23.1",
                 fontsize=10, fontweight='bold')
    ax.legend(fontsize=7); ax.grid(alpha=0.3)
    ax.set_xlabel("x"); ax.set_ylabel("Probability / D(x)")

    # ---- 4: JSD vs KL divergence ----
    ax = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, 3])
    p_vals = np.linspace(0.01, 0.99, 300)
    kl_vals_div = p_vals*np.log(p_vals/(1-p_vals+1e-10)+1e-10) + \
                  (1-p_vals)*np.log((1-p_vals)/(p_vals+1e-10)+1e-10)
    jsd_vals = 0.5*(p_vals*np.log(2*p_vals/(p_vals+1-p_vals+1e-10)+1e-10) +
                    (1-p_vals)*np.log(2*(1-p_vals)/(p_vals+1-p_vals+1e-10)+1e-10))

    ax.plot(p_vals, np.maximum(0, kl_vals_div), '#e84040', lw=2.5, label='KL(p||q)')
    ax.plot(p_vals, np.maximum(0, jsd_vals), '#1a6faf', lw=2.5, linestyle='--',
            label='JSD(p||q) (Eq. 23.11)')
    ax.set_xlabel("p (with q=1-p, binary case)")
    ax.set_ylabel("Divergence")
    ax.set_title("KL vs JSD\n(JSD bounded [0,log2]; KL unbounded)",
                 fontsize=10, fontweight='bold')
    ax.legend(fontsize=9); ax.grid(alpha=0.3)

    # ---- Row 2: Diffusion process visualization ----
    ax = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, :2])
    T = 100
    betas_lin = np.linspace(1e-4, 0.02, T)
    alphas_   = 1 - betas_lin
    alpha_bar = np.cumprod(alphas_)

    t_vals = np.arange(T)
    ax.plot(t_vals, np.sqrt(alpha_bar), '#1a6faf', lw=2.5, label='√ᾱ_t (signal scale)')
    ax.plot(t_vals, np.sqrt(1-alpha_bar), '#e84040', lw=2.5, linestyle='--',
            label='√(1-ᾱ_t) (noise scale)')
    ax.plot(t_vals, alpha_bar/(1-alpha_bar+1e-6), '#2ca02c', lw=2.5, linestyle=':',
            label='SNR = ᾱ/(1-ᾱ)')
    ax.axhline(1.0, color='gray', lw=0.8, linestyle='--', alpha=0.5)
    ax.set_xlabel("Timestep t"); ax.set_ylabel("Scale")
    ax.set_title("DDPM Forward Process (Eq. 23.17-23.18)\n"
                 "x_t = √ᾱ_t x_0 + √(1-ᾱ_t) ε",
                 fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
    ax.legend(fontsize=9); ax.grid(alpha=0.3); ax.set_ylim(0, 1.5)

    # ---- Noising progression ----
    ax = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, 2:])
    # Simulate noising of a 1D signal
    x0_signal = np.sin(np.linspace(0, 4*np.pi, 100)) * 2
    t_checkpoints = [0, 10, 25, 50, 75, 99]
    colors_d = plt.cm.Blues(np.linspace(0.3, 1.0, len(t_checkpoints)))

    for i, t_ck in enumerate(t_checkpoints):
        abar = alpha_bar[t_ck]
        eps  = rng.standard_normal(100)
        x_t  = np.sqrt(abar)*x0_signal + np.sqrt(1-abar)*eps
        ax.plot(x_t + i*7, lw=1.5, color=colors_d[i],
                label=f't={t_ck} (SNR={abar/(1-abar+1e-6):.2f})')

    ax.set_title("Forward Process: Signal → Noise\n(Each trace offset for clarity)",
                 fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
    ax.legend(fontsize=7, ncol=2); ax.grid(alpha=0.3)
    ax.set_xlabel("Position")

    # ---- Row 3: VAE training on 2D Gaussian mixture ----
    # Generate 2D mixture data
    n_data = 500
    centers = np.array([[2.,2.],[-2.,2.],[0.,-2.]])
    X_mix   = np.vstack([rng.normal(c, 0.5, (n_data//3, 2)) for c in centers])

    vae = VAE(d_x=2, d_z=2, d_h=32, beta=1.0, seed=42)
    hist = vae.fit(X_mix, n_epochs=80, lr=5e-3, batch_size=64)

    ax = fig.add_subplot(gs[2, 0])
    ax.plot(hist['elbo'], '#1a6faf', lw=2, label='ELBO')
    ax.plot([-e for e in hist['recon']], '#e84040', lw=2, linestyle='--', label='-Recon')
    ax.plot(hist['kl'],   '#2ca02c', lw=2, linestyle=':', label='KL')
    ax.set_title("VAE Training (Eq. 23.5)\nELBO = Recon - KL",
                 fontsize=10, fontweight='bold')
    ax.set_xlabel("Epoch"); ax.legend(fontsize=8); ax.grid(alpha=0.3)

    # Latent space
    ax = fig.add_subplot(gs[2, 1])
    mu_enc, log_var, z_enc = vae.encode(X_mix, seed=42)
    colors_mix = ['#1a6faf']*167 + ['#e84040']*167 + ['#2ca02c']*167
    ax.scatter(z_enc[:,0], z_enc[:,1], c=colors_mix[:len(z_enc)], s=8, alpha=0.5)
    # Sample from prior
    z_prior = rng.standard_normal((200, 2))
    ax.scatter(z_prior[:,0], z_prior[:,1], color='k', s=5, alpha=0.15, marker='.')
    ax.set_title("VAE Latent Space\n(Colored: encoded data, Gray: prior samples)",
                 fontsize=10, fontweight='bold')
    ax.set_xlabel("z₁"); ax.set_ylabel("z₂"); ax.grid(alpha=0.3)

    # Reconstruction
    ax = fig.add_subplot(gs[2, 2])
    x_recon = vae.decode(z_enc)
    ax.scatter(X_mix[:,0], X_mix[:,1], s=8, alpha=0.4, color='gray', label='Original')
    ax.scatter(x_recon[:,0], x_recon[:,1], s=8, alpha=0.4,
               c=colors_mix[:len(x_recon)], label='Reconstructed')
    ax.set_title("VAE Reconstruction\n(Colored = reconstructed)",
                 fontsize=10, fontweight='bold')
    ax.legend(fontsize=8); ax.grid(alpha=0.3)

    # Generated samples
    ax = fig.add_subplot(gs[2, 3])
    x_gen = vae.sample(n=300, seed=42)
    ax.scatter(X_mix[:,0], X_mix[:,1], s=6, alpha=0.3, color='gray', label='Real data')
    ax.scatter(x_gen[:,0],  x_gen[:,1],  s=6, alpha=0.7, color='#e84040', label='VAE samples')
    ax.set_title("VAE Generation (Eq. 23.3)\nSample z~N(0,I), decode",
                 fontsize=10, fontweight='bold')
    ax.legend(fontsize=8); ax.grid(alpha=0.3)

    plt.suptitle("Module 23: Generative Models — AE, VAE, GAN & Diffusion",
                 fontsize=14, fontweight='bold', y=1.01)
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.savefig("module23_generative.png", dpi=150, bbox_inches='tight')
    plt.show()
    print("Saved: module23_generative.png")

    rng = np.random.default_rng(42)

    X_test = rng.normal(0, 1, (64, 10))

    print(f"  KL loss:     {kl:.4f}")

    vae_2d  = VAE(d_x=2, d_z=2, d_h=32, beta=1.0, seed=42)
    hist    = vae_2d.fit(X_mix, n_epochs=50, lr=1e-2, batch_size=32)
    print(f"\n  Initial ELBO: {hist['elbo'][0]:.4f}")
    print(f"  Final   ELBO: {hist['elbo'][-1]:.4f}")
    print(f"  Final   KL:   {hist['kl'][-1]:.4f}")
    # Sample

    print(f"  Generated samples shape: {x_gen.shape}")

    # --- C: GAN theory ---
    print("\n" + "=" * 58)
    print("  GAN THEORY (Theorem 23.1)")
    print("=" * 58)
    gan = GAN(d_x=2, d_z=4, d_h=16, seed=42)
    # Compute optimal discriminator for two 1D Gaussians
    x_test = np.linspace(-3, 3, 100)
    p_data = np.exp(-0.5*(x_test-1)**2)/np.sqrt(2*np.pi)
    p_gen  = np.exp(-0.5*(x_test+1)**2)/np.sqrt(2*np.pi)
    D_opt  = gan.optimal_discriminator(x_test, p_data, p_gen)
    jsd    = gan.jsd(p_data/p_data.sum(), p_gen/p_gen.sum())
    print(f"\n  Optimal D*(x) range: [{D_opt.min():.4f}, {D_opt.max():.4f}]")
    print(f"  D*=0.5 at x ≈ {x_test[np.argmin(np.abs(D_opt-0.5))]:.3f}")
    print(f"  JSD(p_data || p_G) = {jsd:.4f}")
    print(f"  C(G) = 2·JSD - log4 = {2*jsd - np.log(4):.4f}  (Eq. 23.10)")

    for t_ck in [0, 25, 50, 75, 99]:

        x_t, eps = ddpm.q_sample(x0, t_arr)
        abar = ddpm.alpha_bar[t_ck]

        print(f"  t={t_ck:3d}: ᾱ={abar:.4f}, SNR={snr:.4f}, "
              f"E[||x_t-x_0||²] ≈ {np.mean((x_t-x0)**2):.4f}")

    # Train DDPM briefly
    print(f"\n  Training DDPM ({ddpm.T} steps)...")
    X_ddpm = rng.normal(0, 1, (200, 4))
    X_ddpm[:100] += np.array([2,2,-2,-2])   # bimodal
    losses = ddpm.fit(X_ddpm, n_epochs=20, lr=5e-4, batch_size=32)
    print(f"  Initial loss: {losses[0]:.4f}")
    print(f"  Final   loss: {losses[-1]:.4f}")
    samples = ddpm.sample(n=8, seed=42)
    print(f"  Generated samples: {samples.shape}, "
          f"mean norm = {np.linalg.norm(samples, axis=1).mean():.4f}")

    # --- E: Visualization ---
    full_visualization()
```

$$\log p_\theta(\mathbf{x}) \geq \underbrace{\mathbb{E}_{q_\phi}[\log p_\theta(\mathbf{x}\mid\mathbf{z})]}_{\text{reconstruction}} - \underbrace{D_{KL}(q_\phi|p)}_{\text{KL}} \tag{ELBO, Eq. 23.5}$$ $$D_{KL}(q_\phi|p) = \frac{1}{2}\sum_j(\mu_j^2+\sigma_j^2-\log\sigma_j^2-1) \tag{Closed-form KL, Eq. 23.6}$$ $$\mathbf{z} = \boldsymbol\mu_\phi(\mathbf{x}) + \boldsymbol\sigma_\phi(\mathbf{x})\odot\boldsymbol\varepsilon,\quad\boldsymbol\varepsilon\sim\mathcal{N}(\mathbf{0},\mathbf{I}) \tag{Reparameterization, Eq. 23.7}$$ $$D^_(\mathbf{x}) = p_{\text{data}}/(p_{\text{data}}+p_G),\quad C(G^_) = -\log 4 \tag{GAN optimum, Eqs. 23.9-23.10}$$ $$\mathbf{x}_t = \sqrt{\bar\alpha_t}\mathbf{x}_0 + \sqrt{1-\bar\alpha_t}\boldsymbol\varepsilon \tag{DDPM forward, Eq. 23.18}$$ $$\mathcal{L}_{\text{simple}} = \mathbb{E}_{t,\mathbf{x}_0,\boldsymbol\varepsilon}!\left[|\boldsymbol\varepsilon - \boldsymbol\varepsilon_\theta(\mathbf{x}_t,t)|^2\right] \tag{DDPM training, Eq. 23.20}$$
